items.name: Theorem 1.5 / 8.18: the E^2-page of the mod p descent spectral sequence for TC(O_K)
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Let d = [K(ζ_p):K]. There are explicitly constructed classes β ∈ E^2_{0,2d}(TC(O_K); F_p), λ ∈ E^2_{−1,0}, γ ∈ E^2_{−1,2d+2} and α^{(j)}_{i,l} ∈ E^2_{−1,2j} (1 ≤ i ≤ e_K, 1 ≤ j ≤ d, 1 ≤ l ≤ f_K) such that, as F_p[β]-modules, E^2_{0,*} = F_p[β], E^2_{−1,*} = F_p[β]{λ, γ} ⊕ F_p[β]{α^{(j)}_{i,l}}, E^2_{−2,*} = F_p[β]{λγ}, and E^2_{i,*} = 0 for i ≠ 0, −1, −2; E^2_{0,*} and E^2_{−2,*} are concentrated in even degrees. Consequently the descent spectral sequence converging to TC_*(O_K; F_p) collapses at E^2.
items.locator: Theorem 1.5, arXiv v4 p. 5; Theorem 8.18 and Corollary 8.19, arXiv v4 p. 57
items.note: The main theorem, valid for every p and every K, including p = 2. Assembled from Propositions 8.11, 8.12, 8.14, 8.15, Corollary 6.15 and the multiplicativity of the mod p E^2-pages (Remark 6.1). The identification of d with [K(ζ_p):K] is Proposition 8.23 (item 004). The stated result is retained as a target of the paper. Acceptance of the full local descent proof remains blocked by OPEN-SIGN and OPEN-DESCENT; the review does not infer that the main additive group result is false.

items.name: Theorem 8.20: TC_*(O_K; F_p) for p odd
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Let p be odd and d = [K(ζ_p):K]. Then TC_*(O_K; F_p) ≅ F_p[β]{1, λ, γ, λγ} ⊕ F_p[β]{α^{(j)}_{i,l} : 1 ≤ i ≤ e_K, 1 ≤ j ≤ d, 1 ≤ l ≤ f_K} as F_p[β]-modules, with |β| = 2d, |λ| = −1, |γ| = 2d + 1, |α^{(j)}_{i,l}| = 2j − 1; in particular it is a free F_p[β]-module.
items.locator: Theorem 8.20, arXiv v4 p. 57
items.note: KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.5 plans 'the calculation of THH/TR/TC for … the complete DVRs required for local-field K-theory' (Hesselholt–Madsen's route through log de Rham–Witt). Liu–Wang reprove it from Theorem 8.18 (item 001): for p odd the Moore spectrum is multiplicative, so there are no hidden extensions. The stated result is retained as a target of the paper. Acceptance of the full local descent proof remains blocked by OPEN-SIGN and OPEN-DESCENT; the review does not infer that the main additive group result is false.

items.name: Theorem 8.21: TC_*(O_K; F_2)
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Let p = 2 (so d = 1), with the Bott class β ∈ TC_2(O_K; F_2) and the Z_2[β^4]-module structure from the v_1^4 self-map of 𝕊/2. As Z_2[β^4]-modules, TC_*(O_K; F_2) is isomorphic to F_2[β^2]{1} ⊕ Z/4[β^2]{β} ⊕ F_2[β]{λ, γ} ⊕ F_2[β^2]{βλγ} ⊕ F_2[β]{α_{i,l} : 1 ≤ i ≤ e_K, 1 ≤ l ≤ f_K} if [K:Q_2] is odd, and to F_2[β]{1, λ, γ, λγ} ⊕ F_2[β]{α_{i,l}} if [K:Q_2] is even; |β| = 2, |λ| = −1, |γ| = 3, |α_{i,l}| = 1. Equivalently, the 2-extension of β^k is nontrivial exactly when k is odd and [K:Q_2] is odd; this happens iff Hamilton's quaternions do not split over K.
items.locator: Theorem 8.21 and proof, arXiv v4 pp. 58–59; Remark 8.22, arXiv v4 p. 59
items.note: New for ramified K/Q_2 by this method (previously known through Mitchell's 2-adic K-theory and Rognes–Weibel). L.5 keeps the p = 2 hypotheses 'until a separately proved theorem removes them'. Proof: the 2-extension of β^k is k c̄²β^{k−1}, with c detecting ∂(β)/2 = η; its triviality reduces to whether x² − x = 1 splits over k. The printed degree |α_i| = 2i − 1 is a misprint (recorded under sourceIssues).

items.name: Proposition 8.23: d = [K(ζ_p):K]
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Let d be the least positive integer with p − 1 | e_K d and N_{k/F_p}(μ̄)^d = 1. Then d = [K(ζ_p):K].
items.locator: Proposition 8.23 and proof, arXiv v4 pp. 59–60
items.note: Uses μ = p/N_{K/K_0}(−ϖ_K) and, for d' | d, reduction to a tame, then totally tamely ramified with p − 1 = e_K d_1, then μ = 1 situation, where K(ϖ_K^{1/d_1}) = K_0(ζ_p) by Hensel's lemma. One congruence in the proof is misstated (recorded under sourceIssues). Remark 8.25: the proof uses E_K(0) ≡ p mod p², the normalization forced by Theorem 2.15(4). The stated result is retained as a target of the paper. Acceptance of the full local descent proof remains blocked by OPEN-SIGN and OPEN-DESCENT; the review does not infer that the main additive group result is false.

items.name: Lichtenbaum–Quillen for O_K via TC
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. TC(O_K; F_p) → L_{K(1)}TC(O_K; F_p) ≃ TC(O_K; F_p)[β^{−1}] is 0-truncated; consequently TC(O_K; Z_p) → L_{K(1)}TC(O_K; Z_p) and K(O_K; Z_p) → L_{K(1)}K(O_K; Z_p) are 0-truncated. After base change to K(ζ_p), β is, up to a scalar and higher filtration, the d-th power of the Bott element, and the Bott element is detected by β; d = 1 iff ζ_p ∈ K.
items.locator: Remark 1.7, arXiv v4 p. 5; Remark 8.24, p. 60
items.note: Deduced from Theorem 8.18 in remarks, with the Bott element identification sketched. MotivicEtaleKTheory M.7 and KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.6 plan the K-theoretic statement by the motivic/étale route; the TC-level statement and its derivation from the descent spectral sequence are not planned. A 0-truncated map has homotopy fibre concentrated in degrees ≤0; this does not assert surjectivity on π1. The Bott-localization and trace/localization suppliers must be proved before transferring the statement to K-theory. The stated result is retained as a target of the paper. Acceptance of the full local descent proof remains blocked by OPEN-SIGN and OPEN-DESCENT; the review does not infer that the main additive group result is false.

items.name: Relative topological Hochschild homology THH(A/E)
items.statement: For an E_∞-ring E and an E_∞-E-algebra A, THH(A/E) = A^{⊗_E 𝕋} (the tensor with the circle in E_∞-E-algebras), the universal 𝕋-equivariant E_∞-E-algebra with a nonequivariant map from A; THH(A) = THH(A/𝕊). It is multiplicative: THH(A_1/E_1) ⊗_{THH(A_2/E_2)} THH(A_3/E_3) ≃ THH(A_1 ⊗_{A_2} A_3 / E_1 ⊗_{E_2} E_3).
items.locator: Definition 2.1 and Equation (2.2), arXiv v4 pp. 8–9
items.note: RT.2 constructs THH of E_1-algebras with its circle action; the relative version over an E_∞ base is THH in E-modules. HH = THH(−/Z) is not cyclotomic (Nikolaus–Scholze III.1.10).

items.name: Lemma 2.3: cyclotomic structures on relative THH
items.statement: (1) Let E be an E_∞-algebra in cyclotomic spectra with trivial underlying 𝕋-action. A lift of the augmentation THH(E) → E to a map of E_∞-algebras in cyclotomic spectra determines a lift of THH(−/E) to a functor to E_∞-algebras in cyclotomic spectra, via THH(X/E) ≃ THH(X) ⊗_{THH(E)} E. (2) For a commutative square of such lifts for E_1 → E_2 extending to E_∞-maps E_1 → A_1, E_2 → A_2, the induced map THH(A_1/E_1) → THH(A_2/E_2) is a map of E_∞-algebras in cyclotomic spectra.
items.locator: Lemma 2.3, arXiv v4 p. 9
items.note: Essentially BMS2 Construction 11.5, which the BMS2 extraction routes to RT.6 (PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/107).

items.name: TC^-, TP and TC relative to a cyclotomic base; the Nygaard filtration
items.statement: When Lemma 2.3(1) applies, TC^-(−/E) = THH(−/E)^{h𝕋}, TP(−/E) = THH(−/E)^{t𝕋}, with Frobenii φ_l : THH(−/E) → THH(−/E)^{tC_l} and can : TC^- → (THH^{tC_l})^{h𝕋}, and TC(−/E) = fib(Π_l(φ_l^{h𝕋} − can)). After p-completion TP(−/E; Z_p) ≃ (THH(−/E)^{tC_p})^{h𝕋} and TC(−/E; Z_p) = fib(φ − can : TC^-(−/E; Z_p) → TP(−/E; Z_p)). There are the homotopy fixed point and Tate spectral sequences THH_*(−/E)[v] ⇒ TC^-_* and THH_*(−/E)[σ^{±1}] ⇒ TP_* (|v| = (−2, 0), |σ| = (2, 0), can(v) = σ^{−1}); the Nygaard filtration 𝒩^{≥j} on TP_* is the abutment filtration E^∞_{*,j}, multiplicative, with projections p_j : 𝒩^{≥j}TP_0 → THH_j when the Tate spectral sequence collapses. In the comparison TP(A/E)^∧_p ≃ (THH(A/E)^{tC_p})^{hT} and the resulting p-completed TC fibre formula assume additionally that the underlying spectrum THH(A/E) is bounded below, as required by Nikolaus–Scholze Lemma II.4.2. The local O_K instances satisfy this through connectivity. A displayed spectral sequence is not itself a convergence theorem.
items.locator: Definition 2.4 and (2.5)–(2.9), arXiv v4 pp. 10–11
items.note: RT.2: 'Construct TC, TC⁻ and TP with their comparison maps'; Nikolaus–Scholze Lemma II.4.2 for TP ≃ (THH^{tC_p})^{h𝕋}.

items.name: Proposition 2.10: cyclotomic structures on THH(−/𝕊_{W(k)}) and THH(−/𝕊_{W(k)}[z])
items.statement: There are functorial E_∞-cyclotomic structures on THH(−/𝕊_{W(k)}) (using the E_∞-Frobenius of 𝕊_{W(k)}, which agrees with the p-completed cyclotomic structure of THH(𝕊_{W(k)}) via the augmentation) and on THH(−/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]) (using 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] ≃ 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] with BMS2's cyclotomic structure on 𝕊[z], trivial 𝕋-action and Frobenius z ↦ z^p). THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) ≃ THH(O_K)^∧_p and THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]) ≃ THH(O_K/𝕊[z])^∧_p, and likewise for TC, TC^- and TP.
items.locator: Proposition 2.10, Convention 2.11 and Remarks 2.12–2.13, arXiv v4 p. 11
items.note: The BMS2 extraction routes the cyclotomic structure on THH relative to 𝕊[z] to RT.6.

items.name: Proposition 2.14: the Frobenius on the image of z
items.statement: Under i_C : 𝕊[z]^{h𝕋} → TC^-_0(−/𝕊[z]; Z_p) and i_P : (𝕊[z]^{tC_p})^{h𝕋} → TP_0(−/𝕊[z]; Z_p), the cyclotomic Frobenius satisfies φ(z) = z^p (i.e. φ(z) = can(z)^p).
items.locator: Proposition 2.14, arXiv v4 p. 11

items.name: Theorem 2.15 (Bökstedt, Nikolaus–Scholze): TP and TC^- of F_p
items.statement: THH_*(k) = k[u] with u ∈ THH_2(k) the Bökstedt element. (1) The Tate spectral sequence for TP_*(F_p) and the homotopy fixed point spectral sequence for TC^-_*(F_p) collapse; TP_*(F_p) = TP_0(F_p)[σ^{±1}] and can : TC^-_j(F_p) → TP_j(F_p) is an isomorphism for j ≤ 0. (2) TP_0(F_p) = Z_p, p_0 is Z_p → F_p, and φ is the identity on TC^-_0(F_p) ≅ TP_0(F_p). (3) For every lift u_{F_p} ∈ TC^-_2(F_p) of the Bökstedt element there is a unique v_{F_p} ∈ TC^-_{−2}(F_p) with TC^-_*(F_p) = TC^-_0(F_p)[u, v]/(uv − p). (4) φ(u_{F_p}) = can(v_{F_p})^{−1}.
items.locator: §2, Theorem 2.15, arXiv v4 p. 12
items.note: Cited from Nikolaus–Scholze Corollary IV.4.16. As in the BMS2 extraction, Bökstedt periodicity is planned in L.5 ('THH/TR/TC for perfect fields').

items.name: Theorem 2.17(1)–(5): THH, TC^- and TP of O_K relative to 𝕊_{W(k)}[z]
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. (1) THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]) = O_K[u] for any lift u of the Bökstedt element. (2) The Tate spectral sequence for TP_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]) collapses and TP_* = TP_0[σ^{±1}], |σ| = 2. (3) TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]) = W(k)[[z]], with p_0 the W(k)-algebra map z ↦ ϖ_K. (4) The homotopy fixed point spectral sequence collapses, can induces TC^-_j ≅ 𝒩^{≥j}TP_j for all j, and can is an isomorphism for j ≤ 0. (5) The Frobenius φ : TC^-_0 → TP_0 is the Frobenius of W(k) with z ↦ z^p.
items.locator: Theorem 2.17(1)–(5) and proof, arXiv v4 pp. 12–14
items.note: From BMS2 Proposition 11.10 by Proposition 2.10's completions; the BMS2 extraction routes that proposition to RT.6 (PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/109).

items.name: Theorem 2.17(6): the normalization uv = E_K(z) with E_K(0) = p
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. For any u_{F_p} as in Theorem 2.15 there are unique u ∈ TC^-_2(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]) lifting u_{F_p}, v ∈ TC^-_{−2} and σ ∈ TP_2 with φ(u) = σ, can(v) = σ^{−1}, TP_* = TP_0[σ^{±1}] and TC^-_* = TC^-_0[u, v]/(uv − E_K(z)), where E_K is normalized by E_K(0) = p. Consequently the Nygaard filtration on TP_0 = W(k)[[z]] is 𝒩^{≥2j} = 𝒩^{≥2j−1} = (E_K(z))^j for j ≥ 0.
items.locator: Definition 2.16, Theorem 2.17(6) and proof, Convention 2.19, arXiv v4 pp. 12–14; Remark 8.25, arXiv v4 p. 60
items.note: BMS2's argument gives uv = λ(z)E_K(z) for a unit λ; comparing with F_p via z ↦ 0 and Theorem 2.15 shows λ(0) = 1, and a unit b with λ = φ(b)/b rescales (u, v, σ). Remark 8.25: this normalization agreeing with E_K(0) = p is equivalent to Theorem 2.15(4). The printed proof mixes primed and tilded symbols (recorded under sourceIssues). The lift of u_Fp is through its image in TC^-_2(k) along F_p→k, then the surjection from TC^-_2(O_K/𝕊_W(k)[z]). No map O_K→F_p is needed. u_Fp is a fixed Z_p-lift, so multiplying it by1+p is not an allowed alternative normalization.

items.name: Proposition 3.1: the cyclotomic structure on THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1])
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Regard O_K as an 𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]-algebra via z_0, z_1 ↦ ϖ_K (and as an 𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, …, z_n]-algebra via all z_i ↦ ϖ_K). THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) ≃ THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0]) ⊗_{THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)})} THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_1]) has a natural structure of E_∞-algebra in cyclotomic spectra; the maps z ↦ z_0, z ↦ z_1 give left and right units η_L, η_R.
items.locator: Proposition 3.1 and the paragraph after it, arXiv v4 p. 14

items.name: Divided power envelopes, their Nygaard (PD) filtration, and divided power algebras
items.statement: For a commutative ring R and ideal I, D_R(I) is the universal R-algebra equipped with divided powers on the ideal generated by the image of I. Its PD filtration is generated in weight ≥j by products of divided powers of total weight ≥j. In the paper’s original doubled indexing N^{≥2j}=N^{≥2j−1}. Complete with respect to this filtration when writing D_R(I)^∧_N; distinguish it from p-adic completion.
items.locator: §3, statement of Theorem 3.2 and §1, arXiv v4 p. 15; Appendix A, arXiv v4 p. 62
items.note: CR.0 plans PD envelopes over a PD base with explicit envelopes for polynomial regular immersions and PD filtrations. Mathlib has the DividedPowers structure (Mathlib/RingTheory/DividedPowers/Basic.lean:78) and the free divided power algebra DividedPowerAlgebra (Mathlib/RingTheory/DividedPowerAlgebra/Init.lean:100, as a quotient ring, without its divided power structure), but not envelopes. Imports items067–068. CR.0 owns the envelope universal property and DD.1 the completed filtered algebra. Neither the quotient carrier nor its weak universal property alone is an implemented PD envelope.

items.name: Theorem 3.2 / A.1: Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg for periodic cyclic homology of lci quotients
items.statement: Let R be a commutative Z_p-algebra, I ⊂ R a locally complete intersection ideal and A = R/I, with R I-adically separated and A p-torsion-free. Then HP_0(A/R) is canonically isomorphic, as a filtered ring, to the completion of the divided power envelope D_R(I) with respect to its Nygaard filtration (𝒩^{≥2j}D_R(I) = 𝒩^{≥2j−1}D_R(I) the R-span of the I^{[l]}, l ≥ j); the Tate spectral sequence for HP(A/R) collapses at E^2; and HH_*(A/R) ≅ Γ_A(I/I²) as graded rings.
items.locator: Theorem 3.2, arXiv v4 p. 15; Appendix A, Theorem A.1 and proof, arXiv v4 pp. 62–64
items.note: Proof via the Koszul dga R[x]/(x²), dx = a, and Connes' double complex for a principal ideal; tensor products for a regular sequence; Zariski descent in general. Remark 3.3: also obtainable from BMS2's motivic filtration on HP and Bhatt's derived de Rham computation for lci maps.

items.name: Lemma 3.4 and Corollary 3.6: THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) up to associated graded
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Regard O_K as an 𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]-algebra via z_0, z_1 ↦ ϖ_K (and as an 𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, …, z_n]-algebra via all z_i ↦ ϖ_K). Let t_{z_0−z_1} ∈ THH_2(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) = HH_2(O_K/W(k)[z_0, z_1]) ≅ I/I² be the class of z_0 − z_1. The graded ring associated with the u_0-adic filtration of THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) is O_K[u_0] ⊗_{O_K} O_K⟨t_{z_0−z_1}⟩; hence THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) is a p-torsion-free integral domain concentrated in even degrees.
items.locator: Lemma 3.4 and Corollary 3.6, arXiv v4 pp. 15–16
items.note: THH(O_K/𝕊[z_0,z_1])/u_0 ≃ THH(O_K/O_K[z_1]) = HH(O_K/O_K[z]) = O_K⟨t⟩, and the u_0-Bockstein spectral sequence collapses.

items.name: Lemma 3.14: Frobenius divisibility from the Nygaard filtration
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. items.name: The (p, 𝒩)-topology
items.statement: For a ring R with a multiplicative decreasing filtration 𝒩^{≥•}, the 𝒩-topology is the filtration topology, and the (p, 𝒩)-topology has basis of neighbourhoods of 0 the (p^j) + 𝒩^{≥j}, j ≥ 0. Neither is adic in general. TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]) is complete and separated for both, and its Frobenius is continuous for the (p, 𝒩)- but not the 𝒩-topology.
items.locator: Definition 3.16 and Remark 3.17, arXiv v4 p. 17

items.name: Lemmas 3.18–3.19: completeness and continuity of Frobenius on TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1])

items.name: δ-rings
items.statement: A δ-ring is a commutative ring R with a map of sets δ : R → R, δ(0) = δ(1) = 0, δ(xy) = x^pδ(y) + y^pδ(x) + pδ(x)δ(y) and δ(x + y) = δ(x) + δ(y) + (x^p + y^p − (x + y)^p)/p. For p-torsion-free R this is the same as a Frobenius lift φ, via δ(x) = (φ(x) − x^p)/p.
items.locator: §1 and Definition 3.20, arXiv v4 p. 18

items.name: Proposition 3.23: the elements h, δ^k(h) and f^{(k)}
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Regard O_K as an 𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]-algebra via z_0, z_1 ↦ ϖ_K (and as an 𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, …, z_n]-algebra via all z_i ↦ ϖ_K). By Lemma 3.14 there is h ∈ TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) with hφ(E_K(z_0)) = φ(z_0 − z_1) = z_0^p − z_1^p. Define δ^{k+1}(h) = (φ(δ^k(h)) − δ^k(h)^p)/p and f^{(0)} = z_0 − z_1, f^{(k+1)} = (−(f^{(k)})^p + δ^k(h)E_K(z_0)^{p^{k+1}})/p. Then for all k ≥ 0, δ^k(h) ∈ TP_0, f^{(k)} ∈ W(k)[z_0, z_1][h, …, δ^{k−1}(h)] ∩ 𝒩^{≥2p^k}, and δ^k(h)φ(E_K(z_0))^{p^k} = φ(f^{(k)}); moreover f^{(l+1)} = δ(f^{(l)}) − δ^l(h)δ(E_K(z_0)^{p^l}).

items.name: Lemma 3.27: a dense subalgebra
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. items.name: Proposition 3.29: TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) is a δ-ring
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. items.name: Corollary 3.30 and Lemma 3.31: HP of O_K over W(k)[z] and W(k)[z_0, z_1]
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. items.name: Hopf algebroids as cogroupoid objects; filtered and graded freeness
items.statement: A commutative Hopf algebroid is a cogroupoid object in commutative algebras: a cosimplicial algebra A with A^S ⊗_{A^{ {s} }} A^{S′} ≃ A^{[n]} for partitions [n]=S∪S′ with intersection {s}. Write (A^{[0]},A^{[1]}), with two unit maps, coproduct, counit and conjugation. Use completed tensor products for the complete filtered variant and balanced graded tensor products for the graded variant.
items.locator: §4, Equation (4.1) and Convention 4.10, arXiv v4 pp. 22,24

items.name: Proposition 4.4 and Corollary 4.5: flatness of the units
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Both η_L and η_R exhibit TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) as a free and locally finite filtered TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z])-module, and THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) as a free and locally finite graded THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z])-module; in particular both are completely flat.

items.name: Lemma 4.8 and Corollary 4.9: the Hopf algebroids of THH_* and TP_0
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. For 0 ≤ i ≤ n the maps THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_0, …, z_i]) ⊗_{THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_i])} THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_i, …, z_n]) → THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_0, …, z_n]) and TP_0(O_K/𝕊[z_0, …, z_i]) ⊗̂_{TP_0(O_K/𝕊[z_i])} TP_j(O_K/𝕊[z_i, …, z_n]) → TP_j(O_K/𝕊[z_0, …, z_n]) are isomorphisms (all over 𝕊_{W(k)}). Hence THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗•}) and TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗•}) are Hopf algebroids in graded rings and in complete filtered rings respectively.

items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. items.name: Proposition 5.5 and Corollary 5.9: descent along 𝕊_{W(k)} → 𝕊_{W(k)}[z]
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Write 𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗[n]} for the (n+1)-fold tensor power over 𝕊_{W(k)}, so THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗[n]}) = THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, …, z_n]). The 𝕊_{W(k)}[z]-Adams resolution 𝕊_{W(k)} → 𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗•} induces an augmented cosimplicial E_∞-algebra in cyclotomic spectra THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) → THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗•}), and THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) ≃ lim_Δ THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗•}); likewise TC^-(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) ≃ lim_Δ TC^-(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗•}) and TP(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) ≃ lim_Δ TP(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗•}). More precisely the fibre of THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) → lim_{Δ^{≤n}} is n-connected.
items.locator: (5.1)–(5.4), Proposition 5.5 and Corollary 5.9 with proofs, arXiv v4 pp. 25–27
items.note: Uses Mathew–Naumann–Noel, Nilpotence and descent, Proposition 2.14 (the fibre of the n-th partial totalization is the (n+1)-fold smash power of the 0-connected fibre of THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) → THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z])); for TP, homotopy orbits commute with finite limits and the connectivity passes through. The descent along 𝕊_{W(k)} → 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] was suggested by Hesselholt.

items.name: The descent spectral sequences for THH, TC^-, TP and TC of O_K
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Write 𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗[n]} for the (n+1)-fold tensor power over 𝕊_{W(k)}, so THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗[n]}) = THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, …, z_n]). The coskeleton filtrations of Proposition 5.5 give multiplicative second-quadrant spectral sequences E^1_{i,j} = THH_j(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗[−i]}) ⇒ THH_{i+j}(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}), and likewise for TC^- and TP. By Lemma 4.8 and Corollary 4.5, E^1 is the cobar complex of the Hopf algebroid (THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]), THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1])), resp. row by row of (TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]), TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1])), so E^2_{i,j}(THH) = Ext^{−i,j}_{THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_0,z_1])}(THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z])) and E^2_{i,j}(TP) = Ext^{−i}_{TP_0(O_K/𝕊[z_0,z_1])}(TP_j(O_K/𝕊[z])) (comodule Ext). Setting TC(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)})_{(n)} = fib(can − φ : lim_{Δ^{≤n}} TC^- → lim_{Δ^{≤n−1}} TP) gives the descent spectral sequence for TC, whose E^1 is the total complex of E^1(TC^-) → E^1(TP), with an auxiliary spectral sequence Ẽ^2_{i,k,j} ⇒ E^2_{i−k,j}(TC), Ẽ^2_{i,0,j} = ker(can − φ) and Ẽ^2_{i,1,j} = coker(can − φ) on E^2. Geometrically, E^2_{i,j}(TP) = H^{−i}(𝒳, 𝒪_𝒳(j/2)) for the stack 𝒳 = colim_{Δ^op} Spec TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗[n]}).
items.locator: §1, (1.1)–(1.2), arXiv v4 pp. 2–3, and Relation with other works, p. 8; §5, pp. 26–28
items.note: The central construction of the paper, an Adams-type spectral sequence in cyclotomic spectra. §1 conjectures that 𝒳 is the Cartier–Witt stack WCart_{O_K} of Bhatt–Lurie, and that the E^2-page agrees with that of the Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze motivic spectral sequence built from a quasisyntomic perfectoid resolution; neither is proved.

items.name: Proposition 5.14: the Ext computing E^2(THH(O_K))
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Let D_0 : THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) → THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]) be the left-linear map with D_0(t_{z_0−z_1}) = 1 and D_0(t^{[i]}_{z_0−z_1}) = 0 for i ≠ 1. Then Ext_{THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_0,z_1])}(THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z])) is the cohomology of THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z]) → THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z]) dz, a ↦ (D_0 ∘ η_R)(a) dz, |dz| = 2, obtained from the relative injective resolution 0 → THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z]) → THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_0,z_1]) → THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_0,z_1]) dz → 0 given by the divided-power derivative D(t^{[i]}) = t^{[i−1]}. Here the resolution and its maps live in the category of Γ-comodules, where Γ=THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_0,z_1]); D is left A-linear and a comodule morphism, not Γ-linear as an ordinary module map. The derived Ext/cobar comparison requires the flat Hopf-algebroid and relative-injective hypotheses.
items.locator: Equation (5.13), Proposition 5.14 and Equations (5.15)–(5.18), arXiv v4 pp. 28–29

items.name: Corollary 5.19 (Lindenstrauss–Madsen): THH_*(O_K)
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Ext^{0,0}_{THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z_0,z_1])}(THH_*(O_K/𝕊[z])) ≅ O_K, Ext^{1,2n} ≅ O_K/(nE'_K(ϖ_K)) for n ≥ 1, and all other Ext groups vanish; the descent spectral sequence for THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) collapses at E^2. Hence THH_0(O_K; Z_p) = O_K, THH_{2n−1}(O_K; Z_p) ≅ O_K/(nE'_K(ϖ_K)) for n ≥ 1, and the other groups vanish.
items.locator: Corollary 5.19 and Remark 5.20, arXiv v4 pp. 29–30
items.note: Recovers Lindenstrauss–Madsen (TAMS 2000); Krause–Nikolaus give another descent proof. L.5 plans THH of the complete DVRs needed for local-field K-theory; the proof here is a two-term Ext computation (Proposition 5.14, item 037).

items.name: The algebraic Tate and algebraic homotopy fixed point spectral sequences
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. The Nygaard filtration on the rows of E^1(TP(O_K)) and E^1(TC^-(O_K)) gives multiplicative spectral sequences E^1_{i,j,k} = H^i(Gr^{2k} TP_j(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗•})) ⇒ E^2_{−i,j}(TP(O_K)) (algebraic Tate) and the same with TC^- (algebraic homotopy fixed points), with d^r : E^r_{i,j,k} → E^r_{i+1,j,k+r}, one row j at a time; E^1_{i,j,k}(TP) = E^2_{−i,2k}(THH(O_K))σ^{j/2} for j even and 0 for j odd, and the algebraic homotopy fixed point spectral sequence is a truncation of the algebraic Tate one.
items.note: By Remark 3.8 (item 018) the Tate spectral sequences of all TP(O_K/𝕊[z_0, …, z_n]) collapse, so E^2(THH(O_K))[σ^{±1}] ⇒ E^2(TP(O_K)). This replaces the topological Tate differentials of earlier work by algebraic ones. The differential changes filtration k to k+r. It is not an endomorphism of a single k-piece as the subsequent printed display on p30 suggests. The introduction’s diagram on p6 uses E2 correctly.

items.name: Proposition 5.23: E^2(TC^-(O_K)) and E^2(TP(O_K)) have two columns
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. E^2(TC^-(O_K)) and E^2(TP(O_K)) are concentrated in the columns E^2_{0,*} and E^2_{−1,*}; hence the descent spectral sequences for TC^-(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) and TP(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}) collapse at E^2.
items.locator: Proposition 5.23, arXiv v4 p. 30; Remark 1.4, p. 5
items.note: The two-column conclusion uses Corollary5.19 and the convergent filtered-complex construction. Remark1.4 gives its geometric interpretation.

items.name: The mod p descent spectral sequences and their multiplicativity
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Write 𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗[n]} for the (n+1)-fold tensor power over 𝕊_{W(k)}, so THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗[n]}) = THH(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, …, z_n]). THH_*, TP_* and TC^-_* of O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗[n]} are p-torsion-free, so their mod p versions are the reductions mod p, and the coskeleton filtrations give descent spectral sequences E^1_{i,j} = THH_j(O_K/𝕊[z]^{⊗[−i]}; F_p) ⇒ THH_{i+j}(O_K; F_p), and likewise for TP, TC^- and TC (with Ẽ^2_{i,0,j} = ker(can − φ), Ẽ^2_{i,1,j} = coker(can − φ)); E^2 is comodule Ext over the mod p Hopf algebroids. Although the mod p Moore spectrum, hence THH(O_K; F_p), TC(O_K; F_p) etc., is multiplicative only for p ≠ 2, the E^1- and E^2-pages of all the mod p descent spectral sequences are multiplicative for every p.
items.locator: §6, opening paragraphs and Remark 6.1, arXiv v4 pp. 31–32
items.note: The multiplicativity for p = 2 holds because the descent spectral sequences of O_K are multiplicative and the reductions of the E^1-terms are surjective; this is what lets the method reach p = 2, where the Toda bracket ⟨2, η, 2⟩ ≠ 0 obstructs earlier approaches.

items.name: Proposition 6.2: the E^2-page of the mod p descent spectral sequence for THH(O_K)
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Here THH_*(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]; F_p) = k[z]/(z^{e_K})[u]. (1) E^2_{0,*}(THH(O_K); F_p) has k-basis z^l u^n with 1 ≤ l ≤ e_K − 1 or p | e_K n if e_K > 1, and u^n with p | n if e_K = 1. (2) E^2_{−1,*} has k-basis the cycles z_1^l(u_0^{n−1}t_{z_0−z_1} − (n−1)E'_K(z_0)u_0^{n−2}t^{[2]}_{z_0−z_1}) with 0 ≤ l ≤ e_K − 2 or p | e_K n if e_K > 1, and the reductions of u^{(n)} = Σ_{j=1}^{n} ((n−1)!/(n−j)!)(−E'_K(z))^{j−1}u_0^{n−j}t^{[j]}_{z_0−z_1} = (u_0^n − u_1^n)/(nE'_K(z)) with p | n if e_K = 1. (3) E^2_{i,*} = 0 for i ≠ 0, −1. The degree-zero-column monomials have n≥0 and 0≤l≤e_K−1; the degree-minus-one-column cycles have n≥1 and the same ambient l-range, with the displayed alternatives imposing the remaining restrictions.
items.locator: Proposition 6.2 and proof, (6.3)–(6.6), arXiv v4 pp. 33–34
items.note: Via the two-term complex f(u) ↦ −e_K μ̄ z^{e_K−1} f'(u) dz and the comparison map u^n dz ↦ u^{(n+1)}. Remark 6.7: the 'accidental' filtration clash of z^{me_K} ↦ me_K μ̄ z^{me_K−1}dz motivates the refined Nygaard filtration. The e_K = 1 case of (2) and the orientation of the comparison square carry misprints (recorded under sourceIssues).

items.name: The refined Nygaard filtration
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Rescale Nygaard indices by 2 (𝒩^{≥j} now means the old 𝒩^{≥2j}). For a filtered TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]; F_p) = k[[z]]-module M with a Z-indexed filtration 𝒩^{≥•}, the refined filtration is indexed by (1/e_K)Z: 𝒩^{≥j+m/e_K}M = z^m 𝒩^{≥j}M + 𝒩^{≥j+1}M for j ∈ Z and 0 ≤ m < e_K. It restricts to the original filtration on Z, and it is multiplicative if 𝒩^{≥•} is (since z^{e_K} ≡ μ^{−1}E_K(z) mod p).
items.locator: Convention 6.8, Definition 6.9 and Lemma 6.10, arXiv v4 p. 34
items.note: Applied to TP_*(O_K/𝕊[z]^{⊗•}; F_p) and TC^-_* via the left unit; refining via η_L or η_R gives the same filtration since z_0^m − z_1^m ∈ 𝒩^{≥1}. The authors stress it has no topological analogue.

items.name: Lemma 6.11: the associated graded Hopf algebroid of the refined Nygaard filtration
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. The associated graded of the refined Nygaard filtration on (TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]; F_p), TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]; F_p)) is (k[z], k[z_0] ⊗_k k⟨t_{z_0−z_1}⟩), with Δ(t^{[i]}) = Σ_{0≤j≤i} t^{[j]} ⊗ t^{[i−j]} and ε(t^{[0]}) = 1 and ε(t^{[i]}) = 0 for i>0; if e_K = 1 then z_1 = z_0 − t_{z_0−z_1}, and if e_K > 1 then z_1 = z_0 and it is the Hopf algebra (k[z], k[z] ⊗_k k⟨t_{z_0−z_1}⟩).
items.locator: Lemma 6.11, arXiv v4 p. 35

items.name: The refined algebraic Tate and refined algebraic homotopy fixed point spectral sequences
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. The refined Nygaard filtration on E^1(TP(O_K); F_p) and E^1(TC^-(O_K); F_p) gives multiplicative spectral sequences Ẽ^{1/e_K}_{i,j,k} = H^i(Gr^k TP_j(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z]^{⊗•}; F_p)) ⇒ E^2_{−i,j}(TP(O_K); F_p) (and the same with TC^-), with k and the page index r in (1/e_K)Z and d^r : Ẽ^r_{i,j,k} → Ẽ^r_{i+1,j,k+r}; Ẽ^{1/e_K}(TP) is the cohomology of the associated graded cobar complex of k[z][σ^{±1}] over the Hopf algebroid of Lemma 6.11, and Ẽ^{1/e_K}(TC^-) is a truncation of it.
items.locator: §6, paragraph after Lemma 6.11, arXiv v4 p. 35

items.name: Lemma 6.12 and Corollary 6.17: the first pages of the refined algebraic Tate spectral sequence
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. (1) If e_K > 1, Ẽ^{1−1/e_K}_{*,j,*}(TP(O_K); F_p) = k[z]σ^j ⊕ k[z_0]σ^j dz with d^{1−1/e_K}(zσ^j) = σ^j dz, where dz denotes t_{z_0−z_1}. (2) If e_K = 1, Ẽ^1_{*,j,*}(TP(O_K); F_p) = k[z^p]σ^j ⊕ z_0^{p−1}k[z_0^p]σ^j dz, where z_0^{n−1}dz denotes the cycle Σ_{j=1}^{n} ((n−1)!/(n−j)!)(−1)^{j−1} z_0^{n−j}t^{[j]}_{z_0−z_1}, formally (z_0^n − z_1^n)/n. (3) Ẽ^{1/e_K}_{i,*,*} = 0 for i ≠ 0, 1.
items.locator: Lemma 6.12 and proof, Convention 6.16 and Corollary 6.17, arXiv v4 pp. 35–37
items.note: The printed statement and convention carry sign and index slips in the e_K = 1 cycle (recorded under sourceIssues); the form above is the one the proof gives. The displayed σ^j formulas refer to topological degree2j; use that reindexing explicitly. Fix d=η_L−η_R when writing d(z)=+dz, and change the comparison-map signs coherently. E7 and E28 record the incompatible printed conventions; a single isolated arrow correction does not settle all subsequent formulas.

items.name: Corollary 6.15: the mod p descent spectral sequences for TC^- and TP collapse
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. E^2(TC^-(O_K); F_p) and E^2(TP(O_K); F_p) are concentrated in E^2_{0,*} and E^2_{−1,*}; hence the mod p descent spectral sequences for TC^-(O_K; F_p) and TP(O_K; F_p) collapse at E^2.
items.locator: Corollary 6.15, arXiv v4 p. 36
items.note: The stated result is retained as a target of the paper. Acceptance of the full local descent proof remains blocked by OPEN-SIGN and OPEN-DESCENT; the review does not infer that the main additive group result is false.

items.name: Lemmas 6.19–6.20: ξ_0 and the first Frobenius congruence
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Let f^{(0)} = z_0 − z_1, ξ_0 = −δ(f^{(0)})/f^{(0)} and μ̃ = −μ^p/δ(E_K(z_0)). Then ξ_0 ∈ TP_0(O_K/𝕊_{W(k)}[z_0, z_1]) and ξ_0 ≡ −z_0^{p−1} mod (p, 𝒩^{≥(p−2)/e_K+1}); in particular ξ_0 ∈ (p, 𝒩^{≥(p−1)/e_K}). Moreover φ(f^{(0)}) ≡ −μ̃ z_0^{pe_K+p−1} f^{(0)} mod (p, 𝒩^{≥2p}) (refined, rescaled indices).
items.locator: Lemmas 6.19–6.20 with proofs, arXiv v4 pp. 37–38
items.note: Uses hφ(E_K(z_0)) = φ(f^{(0)}) and f^{(1)} = δ(f^{(0)}) − hδ(E_K(z_0)) ∈ 𝒩^{≥p} from Proposition 3.23 (item 024). The proof of Lemma 6.19 has an exponent slip (recorded under sourceIssues). For p=3, δ(z0−z1)=z0 z1(z0−z1) exactly. The corrected first congruence is integral modulo the stated ideal. These local corrections do not certify every iterated differential below.

items.name: Lemmas 6.23, 6.28 and 6.29: Frobenius iterates of z_0 − z_1 modulo p
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. With μ̃ as above: if p > 2 and e_K > 1, then for l ≥ 1, φ^l(f^{(0)}) ≡ (−μ̃)^{(p^l−1)/(p−1)} z_0^{(pe_K+p−1)(p^l−1)/(p−1)} f^{(0)} mod (p, 𝒩^{≥p^l(1+1/(p−1)+1/e_K)}). items.name: Proposition 7.1: E^2_{0,*}(TP(O_K); F_p) and E^2_{0,*}(TC^-(O_K); F_p)

items.name: Corollary 8.6: Frobenius against the refined Nygaard filtration
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. items.name: Lemma 8.10: a twisted Frobenius linear map on a finite field
items.statement: Let k be a finite field of characteristic p with absolute Frobenius φ, and b ∈ k^×. The F_p-linear map bφ − id : k → k is bijective if N_{k/F_p}(b) ≠ 1; otherwise its kernel and cokernel are both isomorphic to F_p.

items.name: Lemma 8.13 and Proposition 8.14: γ and the cokernel of can − φ in column −1
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. There is γ ∈ ker(can − φ) ⊆ E^2_{−1,2(d+1)}(TC^-(O_K); F_p) detected by μ̄^{pd/(p−1)}z^{pe_K d/(p−1)−1}σ^{d+1}dz, and Ẽ^2_{−1,1,*}(TC(O_K); F_p) is a free F_p[β]-module of rank 1 generated by can(γ) ∈ E^2_{−1,2(d+1)}(TP(O_K); F_p).
items.locator: Lemma 8.13, Proposition 8.14 and proofs, arXiv v4 pp. 54–55
items.note: γ is built from the leading term by Proposition 8.4 and corrected in higher filtration by Corollary 8.8; a class of the cokernel of highest leading term must sit on the critical line, where Lemma 8.10 applies. The stated result is retained as a target of the paper. Acceptance of the full local descent proof remains blocked by OPEN-SIGN and OPEN-DESCENT; the review does not infer that the main additive group result is false.

items.name: Proposition 8.15: the kernel of can − φ in column −1 and the classes α^{(j)}_{i,l}
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k, ramification index e_K and residue degree f_K, ϖ_K a uniformizer, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], E_K(z) the minimal polynomial of ϖ_K over K_0 normalized so that E_K(0) = p (its leading coefficient μ is a unit, in general ≠ 1), 𝕊_{W(k)} the spherical Witt vectors, and O_K an E_∞-algebra over 𝕊_{W(k)}[z] = 𝕊_{W(k)} ⊗ 𝕊[z] via z ↦ ϖ_K. Ẽ^2_{−1,0,*}(TC(O_K); F_p) is a free F_p[β]-module with basis γ together with cycles detected by c z^{(pe_K(j−1)+bp^l)/(p−1)−1}σ^j dz ∈ E^2_{−1,2j}(TC^-(O_K); F_p), for l ≥ 0 and 0 < b < pe_K, p ∤ b, b ≡ −e_K(j−1) mod p − 1, p^{l−1} ≤ e_K j/(pe_K − b) < p^l, 1 ≤ j ≤ d, and c running over an F_p-basis of k. For 1 ≤ i ≤ e_K and 1 ≤ j ≤ d there is exactly one b ∈ [p(i−1) + 1, pi−1], hence one (b, l), satisfying these conditions; α^{(j)}_{i,l} (1 ≤ l ≤ f_K) denote the corresponding cycles, of bidegree (−1, 2j).
items.locator: Proposition 8.15 and proof, Remark 8.17 and the paragraph after it, arXiv v4 pp. 55–57
items.note: α ↦ α_1 identifies ker(can) with ker(can − φ) preserving leading terms, using α_2 = Σ_{i≥1}(can^{−1}φ)^i(α_1) where φ raises the filtration (Corollary 8.6). The stated result is retained as a target of the paper. Acceptance of the full local descent proof remains blocked by OPEN-SIGN and OPEN-DESCENT; the review does not infer that the main additive group result is false.

items.name: Divided-power structures on an ideal
items.statement: DividedPowers I assigns γ_n(x) with γ_0(x)=1 for x∈I, γ_1(x)=x, membership, additive, scalar, product and composition identities. Operations outside I follow Mathlib’s zero convention.
items.locator: §3 before Theorem3.2, p15; pinned Basic.lean:78
items.note: Existing ideal-level structure; not an envelope.

items.name: The divided-power algebra carrier and generators
items.statement: For a commutative semiring R and R-module M, DividedPowerAlgebra R M is the quotient by the divided-power generator relations, with dp R n m and weak universality toward an algebra with specified divided powers.
items.locator: §3 p15; pinned Init.lean:100,131,347
items.note: Read carrier/generator declarations; the completed PD-envelope identification remains item015.

items.name: Cyclic multiplicative Hilbert 90
items.statement: For a finite cyclic Galois extension L/K and a chosen generator g of Gal(L/K), norm(x)=1 implies x=y/g(y) for some unit y.
items.locator: Lemma8.10 input, p54; pinned Hilbert90.lean:134
items.note: Preserve finite Galois and generator hypotheses.

items.name: Frobenius fixed field and finite-dimensional kernel/cokernel dimensions
items.statement: In characteristic p, x belongs to the prime subfield iff x^p=x. For a finite-dimensional linear endomorphism, dim(range)+dim(kernel)=dim(V), and dim(V/range)+dim(range)=dim(V).
items.locator: Lemma8.10 deduction, p54; pinned Finite/Basic.lean:753 and finite-dimensional rank-nullity
items.note: These exact ingredients suffice for the twisted finite-field deduction; the composite item062 remains to implement.

items.name: Coalgebra comodules
items.statement: For an R-coalgebra C and R-module M, a right C-comodule is a coaction M→M⊗_R C satisfying coassociativity and counit.
items.locator: §§4–5, pp22–29; pinned TauCeti Comodule/Basic.lean:50
items.note: Ordinary right coalgebra comodules are present. A flat Hopf algebroid with distinct unit maps is a further construction.

items.name: Cofree coalgebra-comodule adjunction
items.statement: The coaction id⊗Δ makes M⊗_R C cofree, with Comodule.Hom(P,M⊗C)≃LinearMap_R(P,M), inverse (g⊗id)ρ.
items.locator: Equation(5.17), p29, equal-unit coalgebra case; pinned Cofree.lean:131,291
items.note: Use symmetry to compare right/left conventions. This does not supply distinct-unit, graded or completed Hopf-algebroid Ext.

items.name: Algebraic spectral-sequence pages
items.statement: In an abelian category, a spectral sequence consists of page complexes and isomorphisms from each page’s homology to the next page.
items.locator: §§5–6; pinned SpectralSequence/Basic.lean:37
items.note: Rescale rational filtration indices to integers. This carrier contains no convergence or multiplicative tower construction.

items.name: Complete filtered modules and completed tensor product
items.statement: For a nonnegatively filtered commutative ring R, filtered R-modules satisfy F^iR·F^jM⊂F^{i+j}M. Completeness means M≃lim M/F^jM with separation. Filter M⊗_R N by sums of images F^aM⊗F^bN for a+b≥j, then complete.
items.note: General filtered algebra belongs to DD.1; non-adic filtrations require their stated completeness hypotheses.

items.name: Locally finite filtered and graded free modules
items.statement: A filtered basis consists of elements m_i with finitely many of filtration degree below each bound, whose filtered direct sum maps isomorphically after completion. The graded version uses homogeneous n_i, finite below each degree bound, and an actual graded direct-sum isomorphism.
items.locator: Definitions4.2–4.3, p23
items.note: Define the filtration shifts on the free generators explicitly; correct m_i to n_i in Definition4.3.

items.name: Balanced tensor products over a graded ring
items.statement: For graded S-modules M,N, start with the degreewise direct sum of M_a⊗_{S_0}N_b and quotient by the homogeneous relations (s m)⊗n=m⊗(s n) for homogeneous s∈S. The result is the graded S-balanced tensor product.
items.locator: §4 p22; corrected source E17
items.note: Import the existing graded-module/tensor direction. Mathlib GradedAlgebra.baseChange handles scalar extension of a graded algebra; it is not this full construction over a graded base. DD.1 adds completion, not a second graded tensor product.

items.name: Associated graded of locally finite completed tensor products
items.statement: For nonnegative complete filtered R-modules M,N that are free and locally finite with shifted bases, their completed tensor is free and locally finite and Gr(M⊗̂_R N)≃Gr(M)⊗_{Gr(R)}Gr(N). A complete filtered module is free and locally finite iff its associated graded is, with chosen lifts of a homogeneous basis.
items.locator: §4 after Definition4.3, p23
items.note: Use the corrected balanced tensor product and convergent lifting; do not assert this for arbitrary filtered modules.

items.name: Flat Hopf-algebroid comodules, cobar complexes and Ext
items.statement: For a commutative Hopf algebroid (A,Γ) flat over the stated A-unit, construct its comodule category, cofree adjunction and cobar resolution. Prove the relative-injective resolution computes derived Ext under explicit flatness/acyclicity assumptions. Extend to graded and complete filtered contexts with exactness and completed-tensor hypotheses; do not assume completeness defines an abelian category.
items.locator: §4 and §5 pp22–29, especially5.13–5.18
items.note: General supplier shared by Adams descent and the local calculation; import items071–077.

items.name: Adams partial-totalization fibre and convergence
items.statement: For a map A→B in the eligible connective ring-spectrum setting, compare the fibre of A→Tot_n(B^{⊗_A(•+1)}) with the (n+1)-fold tensor power over A of fib(A→B). If that fibre is sufficiently connective, prove its connectivity tends to infinity and the full totalization is A.
items.locator: Proposition5.5 proof, p26, citing Mathew–Naumann–Noel Proposition2.14
items.note: The complete primary proof and precise indexing/connectivity contract remain OPEN-DESCENT; no unrestricted infinite-totalization interchange is assumed.

items.name: Spectral coefficients, Bockstein and convergence
items.statement: Define X/p as the Moore cofiber of p on X, and p-completion by the derived inverse system. Construct Bocksteins, tower exact couples, multiplicativity where available, and convergence under verified connectivity/completeness.
items.locator: §§5–6 pp26–32 and Theorem8.21 pp58–59
items.note: At p=2 this is not an HF_2-module coefficient convention; Z/4 extensions remain possible.

items.name: Spherical Witt vectors and their Frobenius
items.statement: For a perfect characteristic-p field k, construct the p-complete E∞-ring 𝕊_W(k) with π0=W(k) and its Frobenius lift, including the augmentation THH(𝕊_W(k))→𝕊_W(k) as an equivalence after p-completion used in Proposition2.10.
items.locator: §2 pp10–11; Lurie Elliptic CohomologyII §5.2 and Nikolaus–Scholze IV.1.2
items.note: Ordinary Witt-vector algebra is already implemented; this spectrum and coherent Frobenius are the missing relative-THH base.

items.name: The complete flat Hopf-algebroid stack interpretation
items.statement: Construct the stack presented by Spec TP_0 of the Čech nerve, and prove its quasi-coherent descent identifies row2j comodule cohomology with H^{-i}(X,O_X(j)). Respect completion/topology; a formal stack is not an arbitrary ordinary affine quotient.
items.locator: §1 pp2–3 and §5 p27
items.note: The precise complete/derived stack category and QCoh comparison remain OPEN-STACK; item036’s old H^{j−i} indexing was incorrect.

items.name: Cartier–Witt and motivic comparison conjecture predicates
items.statement: Record the proposed identification of the local TP descent stack with WCart_{O_K}, and the proposed equivalence between the resulting descent complex and the BMS motivic-filtration complex. These are conjectural comparison predicates, not proved equivalences supplied by this paper.
items.locator: §1 Relation with other works, pp7–8
items.note: Do not use a conjecture as a prerequisite theorem or fabricate an isomorphism to close a dependency graph.

items.name: The trace cokernel class over Z_p
items.statement: The final paragraph of §9 asserts that λ generates the cokernel on homotopy groups of K(Z_p;F_p)→TC(Z_p;F_p). Specify the degree−1 class and prove all other cokernels vanish using the appropriate connective trace-comparison theorem.
items.note: The paper says one may show this without providing the comparison proof; OPEN-TRACE retains the external supplier obligation.

items.name: Motivic and étale comparison for local fields
items.statement: For a p-adic local field K, construct the étale descent spectral sequence H^{-i}(K,μ_p^{⊗j})⇒π_{2j+i}L_{K(1)}K(K;F_p). The norm-residue theorem identifies the relevant motivic range; preserve low-degree exceptions and the p=2 extension data.
items.note: The d=2 pictures are illustrations, not a proof of a filtered trace comparison for arbitrary schemes.

items.name: Filtration order and its multiplicative bound
items.statement: For a separated decreasing discrete filtration, ν(a)=sup{r:a∈F^r}, with ν(0)=∞. One has ν(ab)≥ν(a)+ν(b); equality requires the product of the two initial forms to be nonzero. In the mod-p divided-power associated graded, t^p=0, so unconditional equality is false.
items.locator: §6 p37, corrected E21
items.note: The specific monomial products used in the differential proof need their own nonvanishing check.

items.name: Two-primary Moore extensions and Bott periodicity
items.statement: For the mod2 reduction of an E∞-ring spectrum, express multiplication by2 on a lifted class through the integral Bockstein and η. Supply the v1^4 self-map of S/2 used for the Z_2[β^4]-module action; do not assume multiplication by β defines a ring structure on X/2.
items.locator: Theorem8.21 proof, pp57–59
items.note: A separate stable-homotopy supplier is required; the source states these inputs without proving them.

items.name: Relative HH of a regular quotient and the Koszul model
items.statement: For a regular sequence generating I⊂R, model A=R/I by the Koszul commutative dg algebra, construct the normalized Hochschild mixed complex with Koszul signs, and compare its shuffle divided powers with Γ_A(I/I²). For HP use product totalization and justify filtration completion.
items.locator: AppendixA pp62–64
items.note: DD.0 supplies the shared Koszul construction; this item owns the HH/HP comparison, not a duplicate complex.

items.name: Collapse of the TC descent spectral sequence
items.statement: Once Theorem8.18’s E2-page and convergence have been constructed, all higher differentials vanish: only columns0,−1,−2 occur, odd rows vanish, and the only possible d2 from column0 lands in an odd row. This identifies the associated graded, not automatically the abutment’s extensions.
items.locator: Corollary8.19, p57
items.note: Separate collapse from Theorem1.5 and the odd-/two-primary extension calculations.

items.name: Finite-field Galois group generated by Frobenius
items.statement: For a finite extension L/K of finite fields, the powers of the q-power Frobenius automorphism, indexed by Fin(finrank K L), biject with Gal(L/K). Thus the Galois group is cyclic with that generator.
items.locator: Lemma8.10 input, p54; pinned Finite/Basic.lean:402
items.note: Supplies the chosen generator hypothesis of item069. The twisted-map deduction item062 is still missing.
